issues.description: Constructor visibility for class Lecture is inconsistent/ambiguous: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) instructs students to "Create a constructor that initializes every attribute" (lines 19-21) but does not specify an access modifier. The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares the constructor with package-private visibility (signature at line 13: "Lecture(String lectureName, ...)") rather than public. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) only contains a TODO for adding the constructor (line 6) and does not provide a signature. This can confuse students about whether the constructor should be public (necessary when instantiating from other packages or from external tests) or package-private, and may lead to access/compilation problems if tests or example usage are placed in a different package.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended visibility explicit. Either (a) change the solution constructor to be public (public Lecture(...)) so it is instantiable from other packages and update the template to show the same signature, and add a short sentence to the problem statement clarifying "Create a public constructor that initializes every attribute (in the order shown in the UML)"; or (b) if package-private is intentional, update the problem statement to state that the constructor should have package-private visibility and ensure any tests or example usage are in the same package. Prefer option (a) to avoid accidental access problems for learners and external tests.
